headline: Welcome to my student portfolio
tagline: IT student at DePaul. Containers, Kubernetes and the web.
about: This galaxy is my portfolio. The planet you start on is home; every planet in orbit around it is one of my projects. The whole thing is one Docker image, built by GitHub Actions and running on Kubernetes.

planets.title: Dockerized Flask To-Do API
planets.summary: A small REST API in a slim, non-root image, with a health check and pytest.
body: My first real Dockerfile: python:3.12-slim, dependencies installed before the code so rebuilds take seconds, and a user with no root rights.
The API keeps its tasks in memory, so they reset when the container restarts. That was a good way to learn what a container's state really is.

planets.title: Compose Stack with a Redis Counter
planets.summary: Two services started with one command, talking by service name.
body: A Flask app and Redis in one compose.yaml. The app finds Redis at the hostname redis, set through an environment variable, never an IP.
Stopping Redis shows the difference between the app being down and one feature being down.

planets.title: CI Pipeline to GHCR
planets.summary: GitHub Actions runs the tests, then builds and publishes an image tagged with the commit.
body: Every push to main and every pull request runs the tests first. Only main publishes, as ghcr.io/<me>/galaxy:sha-<commit>.
It's the same pipeline that built the image you're looking at right now.

planets.title: Kubernetes on kind
planets.summary: A Deployment and a Service on a local cluster, with scaling, a rollout and a rollback.
body: Two replicas behind one Service, a readiness probe on /health, and kubectl rollout undo when a bad image went out.
Deleting a pod and watching the Deployment replace it was the moment Kubernetes clicked for me.

planets.title: Nginx Reverse Proxy Lab
planets.summary: One front door routing paths to three small services.
body: Path-based routing to three upstreams, and a friendly 502 page when one of them is down.

planets.title: Python Data Dashboard
planets.summary: A Jupyter notebook turned into a containerized dashboard.
body: Pinned dependencies, a .dockerignore that keeps the 300 MB dataset out of the build context, and a port published with docker run -p.
